Most mornings, breakfast means managing multiple burners, cooking in batches, and dealing with a stack of cookware afterward. Eggs in one pan, bacon in another, potatoes or pancakes in a third, and if someone wants their eggs cooked differently, out comes yet another pan. The cooking itself isn’t the problem. The cleanup is.

So when Misen released its 11-Inch Square Carbon Nonstick Griddle, I was curious whether it could simplify my morning routine or if it was just a skillet with a different shape.

When Misen launched its first Carbon Nonstick frying pan on Kickstarter, it went viral. The appeal was obvious: home cooks wanted an alternative to traditional nonstick cookware that could handle high heat, stand up to metal utensils, and avoid the coatings many people have grown wary of.

Misen’s Carbon Nonstick technology promises exactly that. The cooking surface is made from nitrided carbon steel with an aluminum core, creating a naturally slick cooking surface without relying on a traditional nonstick coating.

The new Square Griddle brings that same technology to a pan designed for everyday favorites like pancakes, hash browns, grilled sandwiches, burgers, and full breakfasts.

This is part of my hands-on testing of Misen’s lineup. I’ve also reviewed the Deeper frying pan and Misen’s stainless steel food storage, which I covered in my Misenware review.

After several weeks of testing, I wanted to answer two simple questions:

  1. Does Misen’s Carbon Nonstick technology live up to the hype?
  2. Does the Square Griddle offer any real advantage over a traditional skillet?

Read on for my experience with the Misen 11-Inch Square Carbon Nonstick Griddle, including what I liked, what I loved, and where I think there’s still room for improvement.

Key takeaways from my testing

  • The extra room is the real win. I fit four grilled cheese sandwiches on the griddle at once, compared with two in my skillet.
  • Food released easily. Eggs, pancakes, and grilled sandwiches slid right off, and leftover bits rinsed away with minimal effort.
  • Low walls make flipping easy. A spatula slides straight under pancakes and burgers.
  • Metal utensils are fine. Misen says the surface is safe for metal utensils, and I used a metal spatula the whole time.
  • It’s big. With the handle it’s about 19 inches long, so check your storage space.
  • It needs a little oil. Misen’s Carbon Nonstick works best with fat, and the surface darkens over time.
  • It won’t replace your skillet. Sauces, braises, and liquid-heavy dishes still belong in a deeper pan.

Misen Carbon Nonstick Square Griddle key features

The Misen Carbon Nonstick Square Griddle is an 11-inch, low-walled carbon steel pan built to cook several foods at once. These are its three standout features:

  • Spacious 11-inch cooking surface: The square shape provides considerably more usable flat cooking space than a standard round skillet, letting you cook multiple items at once.
  • Low sidewalls: Designed for easy spatula access, so it’s simple to slide under delicate foods, flip, and turn without hitting high pan walls.
  • High-heat and multi-cooktop versatility: Misen says it handles temperatures up to 1100°F and works on gas, electric, and induction cooktops.

I expected to like the nonstick performance, but I didn’t expect this pan to replace my skillet as often as it did.

What makes it different: Think of the Misen Square Griddle as a hybrid between three cookware styles:

  • The easy food release of traditional nonstick cookware
  • The natural seasoning ability and responsiveness of carbon steel
  • The durability and high-heat performance of cast iron

Rather than relying on a synthetic coating, Misen’s Carbon Nonstick is made from nitrided carbon steel and is designed to improve the more you use it.

According to Misen, nitriding is a process that superheats steel in a nitrogen-rich environment to create a durable, corrosion-resistant, and naturally slick cooking surface without added coatings.

How I tested the Misen Square Griddle

I’ve been using the Square Griddle in my own kitchen the same way I would any other pan, and I wanted to find out whether it solved some of my daily cooking frustrations or simply offered a different shape.

How I tested

  • Pan tested: the 11-Inch Carbon Nonstick Square Griddle, from Misen
  • How long: several weeks of everyday cooking in my own kitchen
  • What I focused on: food release, browning performance, heat retention and ease of flipping, cleanup, and how it compares to a traditional skillet
  • Foods: pancakes, eggs, breakfast potatoes, hash browns, grilled cheese sandwiches, quesadillas, tacos, and burgers
  • What I haven’t tested: long-term durability beyond these first weeks, the dishwasher (Misen says to hand wash the pan), and induction cooktops (I cook on gas)
  • Specs: ratings and limits come from Misen’s product page and care guide

What is Misen Carbon Nonstick and how does it work?

Misen Carbon Nonstick is nitrided carbon steel with an aluminum core, designed as a coating-free alternative to PTFE and ceramic nonstick pans. The surface is designed to build seasoning over time through regular cooking and conditioning.

What I like about that is simple: instead of preserving a coating, you’re building a cooking surface.

Traditional nonstick cookware is usually at its best on day one. From that point forward, you’re often trying to prevent the coating from scratching, chipping, or wearing out.

The Misen Carbon Nonstick Square Griddle is designed around the opposite idea. Through regular cooking and seasoning, the cooking surface should improve over time rather than slowly deteriorate. Truthfully, only long-term use will determine how well that promise holds up, but the concept is compelling.

It also changed the way I cook:

  • I don’t worry about scratching a coating.
  • I don’t hesitate to use a metal spatula.
  • I don’t think twice about turning up the heat for burgers.

After several weeks of testing, I found myself reaching for the griddle whenever a skillet started to feel limiting. Meals that normally required cooking in batches felt easier to manage, and I spent less time shuffling ingredients around the pan to create space.

Is the Misen Square Griddle better than a skillet?

For foods that need room to spread out and brown, like pancakes, grilled cheese, and burgers, the Misen Square Griddle is better than a skillet. For sauces, braises, and liquid-heavy dishes, a skillet is still the better tool.

Going into testing, I assumed the Carbon Nonstick surface would be the star of the show. Instead, the biggest surprise was how much I appreciated the additional cooking space.

Whether I was making grilled cheese sandwiches, hash browns, or a full breakfast, I could fit more food in the pan at once and finish cooking everything together instead of working in batches.

For example, I can typically fit two grilled cheese sandwiches comfortably in a skillet. With Misen’s 11-inch square cooking surface, I was able to fit four at once with enough room to flip them easily.

It’s one of those benefits that sounds minor on paper but becomes difficult to give up once you get used to it.

The cooking surface was impressively slick right out of the box. Eggs, pancakes, and grilled sandwiches released easily, and any remaining food bits rinsed away with minimal effort.

If your biggest frustration is constantly running out of room in a skillet, Misen’s Square Griddle offers a genuine advantage. Being able to cook more food at once helped me spend less time managing the stovetop and more time eating when everything was ready all at once.

Why choose this griddle over traditional nonstick cookware?

A coating-free pan like the Misen Square Griddle lets you use metal utensils and high heat without worrying about a coating wearing out.

We’ve established that the extra space of this griddle won me over. But if you’re tired of throwing away nonstick and ceramic pans because they don’t last, me too. I’d also rather keep PFAS-coated cookware out of my kitchen, so a pan with no synthetic coating was a big part of the appeal.

With traditional coated nonstick cookware, you constantly feel like you have to protect the coating:

  • Most makers say to avoid metal utensils.
  • Most say to avoid very high heat.
  • The coating wears away over time, and many pans only last a few years.

You don’t need to worry about preserving a coating with Misen’s Carbon Nonstick Griddle. You’re building a cooking surface every time you cook up some eggs or sear some chicken.

Instead, the Misen Square Griddle is built to last and get better with time. And it welcomes high heat up to 1100°F. Pop it in the oven. You can’t do that with most traditional nonstick pans.

That’s not a subtle difference.

If you want something that’s coating-free and built to last, and you’re tired of tossing worn-out pans, Misen’s Carbon Nonstick is worth trying. For a broader look at what to look for, see our guide to the importance of quality cookware.

What foods are best cooked on the Misen Square Griddle?

The Misen Square Griddle works best for foods that need room to spread out and brown, like grilled cheese, smash burgers, quesadillas, hash browns, and pancakes.

Pancakes, eggs, bacon, and French toast are the obvious choices for this griddle. But it can do much more.

In fact, by the end of testing, I was using it more often for lunch and dinner than I was for pancakes.

Some of my favorite uses included:

  • Grilled cheese sandwiches
  • Smash burgers
  • Philly cheesesteaks
  • Quesadillas
  • Fajitas (try our easy shrimp fajitas)
  • Breakfast potatoes and hash browns
  • Blackened fish
  • Noodle dishes and stir-fries
  • Pizza, flatbreads, and naan

All these foods benefit from room to spread out and brown properly. The larger cooking surface consistently led to better browning, better texture, and fewer meals cooked in batches. Looking for burger ideas? See our unique burger recipes.

What could be better about the 11-inch Misen Square Griddle?

The biggest drawbacks are the long handle, the roughly 19-inch footprint, the need for a little oil, and hand-wash-only care.

No cookware is perfect. My biggest complaint about this griddle is the handle. It’s perfectly functional, but it feels much longer than my other pans.

The larger footprint also takes up more storage space than a traditional frying pan. With the handle, the griddle is about 19 inches long. So if you’re short on cabinet storage, this pan may be hard to store.

The catch: using oil with Carbon Nonstick is important to keep food from sticking and to build up the nonstick surface. If you don’t want to use oil when you cook, this griddle and Misen’s Carbon Nonstick cookware line may not be right for you.

One other thing to note is that this pan can darken and develop a patina as you cook with it. According to Misen, that discoloration is the natural seasoning building up, and it’s normal. So if you like your pans to always look brand new, the change might frustrate you.

Also, the 11-inch size might be too small for you. I’m only cooking for 2, but if you have 3 or more people to cook for, Misen’s larger 13-inch and 18-inch Carbon Nonstick griddles would be ideal.

What surprised me most about the Misen Square Griddle

By the end of testing, I stopped thinking of this griddle as a specialized pan and was reaching for it any chance I got. I came for the naturally nonstick cooking surface that was slick right out of the box, but the extra cooking space won me over.

And I loved how easy it is to flip foods on this griddle with the low walls.

What ultimately surprised me most was how naturally it worked its way into my everyday cooking routine.

For me, that’s the sign of a great piece of cookware.

Misen Carbon Nonstick Square Griddle pros and cons

Pros

  • No synthetic nonstick coating. Misen says the surface is PFAS-free.

Cons

When is a regular skillet better than the Misen Square Griddle?

As much as I’ve enjoyed using the Square Griddle, I don’t see it replacing a skillet entirely.

A skillet is still my preferred tool for:

  • Pan sauces
  • Braises
  • Pasta dishes
  • Liquid-heavy recipes
  • Meals that benefit from deeper sidewalls

A skillet gives you depth. The griddle gives you space and low walls for easy flipping.

I still use both.

Misen Square Griddle final verdict

For me it’s a yes. Especially if you want to ditch disposable nonstick pans and cut down on batch cooking.

After a few weeks of cooking everything from four-at-a-time grilled cheeses to full weekend breakfasts, it’s earned a permanent spot on my stovetop.

It solves two of the biggest headaches of everyday cooking at once:

  • It replaces multiple pans: The 11-inch square surface gives you enough room to cook the whole meal together instead of juggling multiple burners and washing a pile of skillets afterward.
  • It eliminates “nonstick anxiety”: You get easy food release right out of the box, without worrying about metal spatulas, high heat, or a coating wearing out.

For everyone else, the Misen 11-Inch Square Griddle isn’t just a novelty shape. It’s a legitimate upgrade that makes daily cooking faster and a whole lot easier to clean up.

Bottom line: the Misen Square Griddle is best for home cooks who regularly make pancakes, eggs, sandwiches, or burgers for more than one person, and anyone ready to invest in a durable, coating-free pan that gets better with age. If you mostly cook single-serving meals, rely on saucy dishes that need high walls, or want cookware you can toss in the dishwasher, a standard skillet will serve you better.

Misen Carbon Nonstick Square Griddle FAQs

Is the Misen Carbon Nonstick Square Griddle worth it?

Yes, for me. The Misen 11-inch Carbon Nonstick Square Griddle is worth $139 if you cook for more than one person and want a coating-free pan with more flat cooking space than a skillet. If you mostly cook for one, rely on sauces and braises, or want a dishwasher-safe pan, a standard skillet will serve you better.

Is the Misen Carbon Nonstick Square Griddle PFAS-free?

Misen says the griddle’s carbon steel surface is PFAS-free, and describes its Carbon Nonstick line as free of PFAS, PTFE, and PFOA. The griddle uses a nitrided carbon steel surface instead of a synthetic coating. One of the main reasons I tested it is that I’ve been gradually moving away from traditional nonstick cookware.

What is Misen Carbon Nonstick?

Misen Carbon Nonstick is nitrided carbon steel with an aluminum core, designed as Misen’s alternative to PTFE and ceramic nonstick cookware. It develops seasoning through cooking and regular use, and Misen describes it as a surface that becomes increasingly nonstick over time.

Does the Misen Square Griddle require seasoning?

The Misen Square Griddle doesn’t need traditional seasoning, according to Misen. The pan self-seasons as you cook, and Misen recommends conditioning it with a very thin layer of oil to speed that up. Personally, I didn’t find maintenance nearly as intimidating as some traditional carbon steel cookware can be.

How do you condition a Misen Carbon Nonstick pan?

To condition a Misen Carbon Nonstick pan, Misen’s care guide says to heat the clean, dry pan over medium-high heat for 30 to 60 seconds, turn off the heat, add 2 to 3 drops (about ¼ teaspoon) of high-smoke-point oil, and rub it in with a dry paper towel until no oil is visible. Let it cool for about 10 minutes. Misen recommends doing this every time you use the pan, or whenever nonstick performance dips.

Can you use metal utensils on the Misen Square Griddle?

Yes. Misen says Carbon Nonstick cookware is safe for metal utensils, and I used a metal spatula throughout my testing without worrying about scratching a coating. That’s one of the things I enjoyed most about using it.

Is the Misen Square Griddle oven safe?

Yes. According to Misen, the Square Griddle is oven safe up to 1100°F, which is significantly higher than what most traditional nonstick cookware can tolerate.

Can the Misen Square Griddle be used on a grill?

Yes. Misen’s care guide says Carbon Nonstick is heat safe to 1100°F, so it works in the oven and on the grill.

Is the Misen Square Griddle induction compatible?

Misen lists the Square Griddle as induction compatible, and says Carbon Nonstick works on gas, electric, and induction stovetops. I didn’t test it on induction. I cooked on a gas range.

How large is the Misen Carbon Nonstick Square Griddle?

The Misen Carbon Nonstick Square Griddle has an 11-inch square cooking surface. Misen lists it at about 19.4 inches long with the handle and 2.72 pounds, with walls under an inch high (0.78 inch). Misen also offers larger 13-inch and 18-inch griddles, and the 18-inch is $179.

Is the Misen Square Griddle better than a skillet?

For foods that need room to spread out and brown, yes. During testing, I consistently preferred the Misen Square Griddle for grilled cheese sandwiches, breakfast potatoes, burgers, cheesesteaks, and quesadillas. For sauces, braises, and liquid-heavy dishes, I still reach for a skillet.

Is the Misen Square Griddle good for smash burgers?

Yes, very. The Misen Square Griddle’s large cooking surface makes it easy to fit multiple patties while still leaving enough room to maneuver a spatula. Burgers got a nice sear and were easy to flip. It was one of my favorite things to cook on it.

Is the Misen Square Griddle good for families?

Yes, I think this is where the Misen Square Griddle really shines. Being able to make four grilled cheese sandwiches at once instead of working in batches is a good example. If you cook for three or more people, you may want one of Misen’s larger griddles.

What foods does the Misen Square Griddle cook best?

The Misen Square Griddle cooks best foods that benefit from room to spread out and brown properly, like grilled cheese, smash burgers, quesadillas, hash browns, and fajitas. While breakfast foods are the obvious answer, I found myself using it just as often for lunch and dinner.

Is the Misen Square Griddle easy to clean?

Yes. I found the Misen Square Griddle much easier to maintain than I expected. Misen recommends hot water, mild soap, and a soft sponge, with its Salt Method for stuck-on food. In everyday use, cleanup was usually quick and straightforward.

Is the Misen Square Griddle dishwasher safe?

No. Misen says to hand wash the Square Griddle and keep it out of the dishwasher.

Why is my Misen Carbon Nonstick griddle changing color?

A Misen Carbon Nonstick griddle changes color as its seasoning builds up, and that’s normal. Misen says discoloration is the pan’s natural seasoning, and that dark spots are fine as long as the surface stays smooth to the touch. You may notice darker areas, uneven coloration, or a more developed patina over time.

What’s Misen’s warranty and trial policy for the Square Griddle?

Misen offers a 60-day test drive with free returns on the Square Griddle, plus a lifetime warranty against defects.
